text: What is an array, and how do you read an element at a given position?
key_points: contiguous block of memory|index to address arithmetic|constant time access by index|fixed size or resizable

text: What is a data structure, and why does the choice of data structure matter for a program?
key_points: way of organising data|different operations cost differently|trade-offs in time and memory|match structure to access pattern

text: What does LIFO mean, and can you name something in everyday computing that behaves like a stack?
key_points: last in first out|push and pop|undo history or call stack|browser back button

text: In simple words, what is the difference between an O(n) algorithm and an O(n squared) one?
key_points: work grows linearly vs quadratically with input|doubling input doubles vs quadruples the work|matters for large inputs|example such as one loop vs nested loops

text: What does Big-O notation describe, and why do we ignore constant factors when we use it?
key_points: upper bound on growth rate|behaviour as input size grows|constants and lower terms dominated for large n|compare algorithms independent of hardware

text: How does a dynamic array grow when it runs out of space, and what is the cost of appending an element?
key_points: allocate larger block and copy|doubling capacity|amortised constant time append|occasional linear-cost copy

text: When would you choose a linked list over an array, and when would you not?
key_points: cheap insert or delete given a node|no random access by index|extra memory for pointers|poor cache locality

text: Compare a stack and a queue: how do they differ, and where does each appear in real systems?
key_points: LIFO vs FIFO|stack: call stack, undo, parsing|queue: scheduling, buffering, BFS|both can be built on arrays or linked lists

text: How does a hash table handle two keys that map to the same slot, and what happens to performance as it fills up?
key_points: collision handling by chaining or open addressing|load factor|resizing and rehashing|average constant time, worst case linear

text: What is a binary search tree, and what goes wrong when it becomes unbalanced?
key_points: left smaller right larger ordering|search insert delete follow one path|degenerates to a linked list|height decides cost, O(log n) vs O(n)

text: At a high level, how do self-balancing trees such as AVL or red-black trees keep their height small?
key_points: track balance information per node|rotations restore balance after insert or delete|guaranteed logarithmic height|cost is extra bookkeeping

text: What is a binary heap, and how does a priority queue use it?
key_points: complete binary tree with heap property|stored in an array|insert and extract in logarithmic time|peek the min or max in constant time

text: Compare breadth-first and depth-first search: how each traverses a graph, what structure it uses, and when you would pick each.
key_points: BFS uses a queue, DFS a stack or recursion|BFS finds fewest edges in unweighted graphs|DFS for cycles, topological order, components|both visit each vertex and edge once

text: How does Dijkstra's algorithm find shortest paths, and why does it break when edges can be negative?
key_points: greedy choice of the closest unvisited vertex|priority queue of tentative distances|relaxation of edges|settled vertices assumed final, which negative edges violate

text: Compare quicksort and merge sort in terms of time, memory, stability and worst case.
key_points: both n log n on average|quicksort worst case n squared, in place|merge sort stable, needs extra space|pivot choice matters

text: Why can a comparison-based sort not beat n log n, and when is it possible to sort faster?
key_points: decision tree argument gives n log n lower bound|counting or radix sort avoid comparisons|need bounded keys or digits|trade-off is memory and assumptions

text: How does binary search work, what must be true of the data, and where do people usually make mistakes implementing it?
key_points: data must be sorted|halve the search range each step|logarithmic time|off-by-one errors in bounds and midpoint overflow

text: What makes a recursive solution correct, and how can recursion cause a stack overflow?
key_points: base case|each call moves toward the base case|every call uses stack space|convert to iteration or use tail calls where supported

text: What do overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure mean, and how do memoization and tabulation differ?
key_points: subproblems repeat so cache results|optimal answer built from optimal sub-answers|memoization is top down|tabulation is bottom up and avoids recursion

text: How is a greedy algorithm different from dynamic programming? Give one problem where greedy is correct and one where it is not.
key_points: greedy commits to a local best choice|needs the greedy-choice property|example: interval scheduling or Huffman coding|counter-example: coin change with unusual denominations

text: How would you check whether two strings are anagrams, and what are the trade-offs between the approaches?
key_points: sort both and compare|count characters with a hash map or array|linear vs n log n time|extra space and character set size

text: What is a trie, and what is it good at compared with storing strings in a hash set?
key_points: tree keyed by characters|prefix queries and autocomplete|lookup cost depends on string length|higher memory use

text: What does the union-find data structure do, and which optimisations make its operations nearly constant time?
key_points: tracks disjoint sets|find and union operations|path compression|union by rank or size

text: What is the difference between time and space complexity, and between worst-case and amortised cost? Give an example of each.
key_points: time counts steps, space counts memory|worst case is the single most expensive input|amortised averages over a sequence of operations|example: dynamic array append

text: Design an LRU cache whose get and put both run in constant time. Which data structures would you combine, and why?
key_points: hash map for lookup|doubly linked list for recency order|move a node to the front on access|evict from the tail when full

text: You have a map of cities and roads. How would you find the route with the fewest road segments between two cities, and how would your approach change if roads had different lengths?
key_points: model as a graph|BFS for fewest segments|Dijkstra for weighted lengths|track visited and predecessors to rebuild the path

text: A function that checks for duplicates in a list of one million items takes minutes to run. How would you find out why, and how would you fix it?
key_points: profile or reason about complexity|nested loops give quadratic time|use a hash set for linear time|trade extra memory for speed

text: Numbers arrive as a stream and at any moment you must report the k largest. How would you do it and what does each new number cost?
key_points: min-heap of size k|compare new item with the heap minimum|logarithmic in k per item|memory limited to k items

text: Given two strings, how would you compute the minimum number of edits needed to turn one into the other?
key_points: edit distance with insert delete replace|table indexed by prefixes of both strings|recurrence from neighbouring cells|time and space proportional to the product of lengths

text: Design autocomplete for a search box with a million words. Which structure would you use and how would you rank the suggestions?
key_points: trie or prefix index|walk to the prefix node then collect completions|rank by frequency or recency|limit to top k and cache popular prefixes
